claims.text: Coding variants in IL23R (e.g. R381Q) are robustly associated with Crohn's disease risk, with the rare allele conferring protection.
Multiple Th17-pathway genes (IL23R, STAT3, JAK2, CCR6, TYK2) are among the >200 IBD susceptibility loci identified by GWAS meta-analysis.
IL-17A expression is elevated in inflamed mucosa and serum of patients with active Crohn's disease compared with controls.

evidence.excerpt: IL-17A transcripts were increased in inflamed mucosa.

claims.text: IL-17A produced independently of IL-23 by gut γδ T cells regulates occludin localization and maintains intestinal epithelial barrier integrity; its neutralization worsens barrier permeability in mouse colitis models.
Open Targets assigns IL17A a moderate overall association score with Crohn's disease, driven mainly by literature and expression rather than genetics.

analysts.title: Direct evidence: IL-17 blockade in Crohn's disease

claims.text: In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) in 59 patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease, the primary endpoint was not met and the trial was stopped early for futility.
Secukinumab-treated patients had higher rates of adverse events and disease worsening than placebo.
A randomized trial of brodalumab (anti-IL-17RA) in Crohn's disease was terminated early because of disproportionate disease worsening in active arms.
IL-23 p19 inhibitors have shown efficacy in phase 3 Crohn's induction and maintenance trials, indicating the pathway is druggable upstream of IL-17.
Approved IL-17 inhibitor labels warn about new-onset or exacerbated inflammatory bowel disease.
Phase 1 healthy-volunteer data for the asset showed no dose-limiting toxicity; no data exist in patients with active intestinal inflammation.
The Crohn's biologic market is served by anti-TNF, anti-integrin, IL-12/23 and IL-23 p19 agents, with further late-stage entrants in the pipeline.
An IL-17 agent would need a differentiated mechanism or biomarker-selected population to compete against IL-23 p19 inhibitors.
Genetic support for the IL-23/Th17 axis does not transfer to IL-17A blockade: the direct randomized evidence for IL-17 inhibition in Crohn's disease is negative.
Elevated mucosal IL-17A may be protective rather than pathogenic, so expression-based patient selection (mucosal IL17A) is not a validated enrichment strategy.
The company has not presented any mechanism that would avoid the barrier-disruption effect seen with secukinumab and brodalumab.
